concerns.text: T029 implements Ridge regression as a fallback for collinearity (VIF > 5). This violates the data-flow dependency on the Spec/Plan which explicitly mandates PCA or a HALT for collinearity (FR-005, Plan Complexity Tracking). The task order implies a valid execution path (Ridge) that the spec forbids, creating a semantic dependency violation where the consumer (Stats) relies on a producer (Ridge logic) that should not exist.

T032 and T044 define sensitivity analysis sweeping motion and p-values but omit the 'Outcome Definition' sweep (Change vs. Residual vs. Raw Post) mandated by Plan Phase 4 and Spec FR-010/SC-006. The downstream task T045 (Integration Test) and T050 (Final Verification) depend on the full sensitivity artifact (`reports/sensitivity_analysis.md`) which will be incomplete if T032/T044 do not include the outcome sweep. This breaks the producer-consumer flow for the final report.

T001a is marked 'REJECTED' in the prior analysis but remains in the task list as a prerequisite for T012 and T041. A task cannot be a hard dependency if it is rejected/missing. The ordering implies a valid `data/verified_sources.json` exists, but the task to create it is flagged as invalid, breaking the foundational data-flow chain for US1.

T044 is marked 'REJECTED' in the prior analysis but is listed as a dependency for T045 and T050. The integration test (T045) and final verification (T050) cannot validate the sensitivity analysis artifact if the task generating it (T044) is rejected. This creates a circular or broken dependency chain in the execution order.

T001a description implies a single pre-identified ID check, whereas Spec FR-013 and Plan Phase 0.1 mandate an iterative multi-source aggregation loop. The task description does not reflect the full scope of the producer (multi-source search) required before the consumer (download) can proceed.
